content.text: Truco (Argentine) is the national card game of Argentina and one of the most popular in South America. 2-6 players with 40-card Spanish deck. 3 cards each, win 2/3 tricks. Unique card hierarchy (Aâ™  > Aâ™£ > 7â™  > 7â™¦). Three betting lances: Envido (hand value), Truco (trick stakes), and Flor (3 same suit). Heavy bluffing.

Truco is descended from the simpler game Truc (Truque), which originated in parts of Spain (Valencia, Balearic Islands) and Southern France. It spread to South America with colonization and became the national card game of Argentina, with distinct regional forms in Uruguay, Brazil, Chile, and Venezuela. The bluffing, talking, and joking that accompany play are an integral part of its cultural role.
40 Spanish cards (no 8s, 9s, 10s). Special ranking: Aâ™  > Aâ™£ > 7â™  > 7â™¦ > 3s > 2s > False As > 12s > 11s > 10s > False 7s > 6s > 5s > 4s.

Each player is dealt three cards from the 40-card deck; no further cards are drawn during play. The deal rotates counterclockwise; the player to the right of the dealer (mano) plays first, the dealer (pie) plays last.
